review: Reviewed Wren's round-278 request (hand-lash-branches: learn to bind two owned branches at a crossing with an owned handmade fiber cord, then inspect, conservatively hand-test and undo the actual binding; bare hands on dry footing, with nearby space, branch geometry, cord length, condition, friction and grips deciding feasibility; Wren owns two separate 0.34 m reed cords and has collected no branches; inputs are exact owned piece and cord ids, a crossing arrangement and a bounded test force and duration, with no invented tools, anchors, extra cord or branches; costs unknown, actual study and work time charged, paid progress kept and reservations and cancellation disclosed; a physical binding relation without duplicated material, measured geometry and limited test results including slip or damage, inspection and untying, and no strength rating or shelter effect) and the World Agent's develop review (learning 4): a general hand-bind-crossing with modes attempt, inspect, trial, untie and cancel on one work record and contact model, two exact owned rigid-piece ids, one exact owned cord and a crossing pose; one enclosing wrap closed by an overhand in the same cord's ends as a minimal experimental binding, not a rated lashing; study 4 rounds at 0.2 energy; attempt reserves the three inputs and pays four rounds of 0.5 (measure/position, route the wrap, form and tuck the closure, dress and release-check), each persisting its measured geometry; inspect 1 round at 0.2; trial 1 round at 0.5 with force above 0 to 10 N and duration above 0 to 60 s; untie two rounds of 0.5; cancel immediate and free; no material fee, only actual damage; dimensions and condition obtained through paid handling, not invented from the word branch; a wrap centreline from the actual crossing with bend limits and hand clearance, the cord centreline equal to wrap plus closure plus both tails, cord-knot@1 closure constraints, one-person hand feasibility at every stage with no third hand or anchor, and a paid measured shortfall where a route or length fails; a versioned crossing-contact law with explicit cord-to-branch friction not inferred from cord-to-cord friction; a release check of closure retention and contact; a relation of the three original items; an opposed hand-grip trial clear of the crossing with stated grip sites and direction, the minimum of requested, actor, grip and test limits, a recorded force course and refusal of unsupported load modes; relaxation of hand-held geometry on interruption, resume by workId from the last surviving stage, cancel and death rules; cord wear once; later movement resolved through the law; refusal of joined cords as an extended assembly in this minimal version; reusable versioned view metadata and stage, shortfall, routing, closure, release, test, slip, damage, pause, resume, cancel and untie events; no reward, satisfaction, comfort or shelter. The specification is self-consistent and every gated physical transition can be given an explicit declared rule, so this is a simplified real mechanism, not a first release. Implemented hand-bind-crossing@1 in scope long-ex16 (new module packages/world-core/src/long-crossing-binding.ts, export LONG_CROSSING_BINDING, handler long.hand-bind-crossing, events prefixed crossing-binding-, law crossing-contact@1, method single-wrap-overhand-closure), registered at the end of V7_PACKAGES with package dependencies foundation-open@1, hand-twist-fiber-cord@1, hand-tie-cord-knot@1 and hand-join-fiber-cords@1; learning 4 with learningEnergy 0.2, so each study round is paid; no prerequisite, and no cord ability is required; the ability serializes to 3,464 code units within the 3,500 limit; references are empty, so all ids are exact. Modes and costs: attempt (pieceIds: two own untreated branch items, one whole unit each, the first on top; a two-unit lot may be named twice and gives up one unit as a new conserved item, while a single-unit item is reserved in place and keeps its id; cordId: an own straight hand-twist-fiber-cord cord or fragment that is not knotted, joined, bound or reserved; crossingAngle 30-90 degrees) reserves the three items and pays four rounds of 0.5 energy (measure-position, route-wrap, form-tuck-closure, dress-release-check), continuing each round and resumable only by workId; a loose tucked binding left by cancellation or creep needs only the dressing round; inspect (bindingId or workId) costs 0.2 and changes nothing; trial (bindingId, trialForce, trialDuration, trialDirection separate or slide) costs 0.5; untie pays two rounds of 0.5 (withdraw-closure-end, open-remove-wrap); cancel is free. Every validation (mastery, arguments, exact own ids, a rigid-piece law for the pieces and strand and friction laws for the cord, whole units, untreated pieces, no knot, join, binding or reservation, a two-ply section, condition 0.5, the material-independent least cord length, the crossing angle, footing, the work circle, clear dry ground for the crossed pieces in at least one of four directions, energy, no unfinished own work) precedes any charge, so refusals spend nothing; no material is consumed. Modeling assumptions of crossing-contact@1: a piece is one whole branch unit measured in the paid first round under the existing branch values of the open-shelter-material.ts law (version 2), re-stated without calling it as fiber-cord@1 re-states its reed values (one 2 m member, 350 kg/m3 solid, water share 0.5 by the existing hydration rule, 4 GPa modulus, 45 MPa strength weakened by 0.6 x water share), its diameter following from conserved solid volume (31.6 mm for a 1.1 mass unit) and its condition 1 unless damaged here; branch-screen@1's slot sizes, windbreak effect and recovered pieces are not used, and treated or recovered pieces are refused; the pre-cost space check uses that represented 2 m extent; the pieces cross at their midpoints, the first on top, laid on the ground at the person's place with the top piece along the first clear direction of 0, 45, 90 and 135 degrees, resting on the ground for support without any anchor; the cord width w is the fiber-cord@1 grip width and its tightest radius R the cord-knot@1 bend limit measured on the live item; the wrap lies in the plane through the obtuse bisector of the crossing, at beta = (180 - angle)/2 to both axes, each section is an ellipse with semi-axes r/sin beta and r offset by w/2, and the wrap centreline is two half Ramanujan perimeters plus two straight sides; where a section's tightest radius b^2/a is below R the cord bridges and touches over that share of its half turn; routing adds a 0.02 m fingertip opening on each side (0.04 m); the closure is an overhand in the two ends (a half knot over the top piece) whose ends each turn half round the other at Rc = max(R, w), path pi Rc + w per end, formed at max(Rc, (0.02 m + w)/2) with a 0.02 m pinch beyond it and seated with retained tails of 0.02 m + w (cord-knot@1 rules), the method sharing the remainder equally between the tails; one hand holds the crossing while the other routes, so a stack thicker than 0.1 m (an assumed one-hand span) or a lift of both pieces above half the fiber-cord@1 200 N two-hand pull scaled by health is a paid measured shortfall, and closing and dressing use both hands while the pieces rest on the ground; closure retention reuses cord-bend@1's reed-on-reed friction 0.3 and tail rule (each end turns pi x min(1, w/Rc) round the other and is nipped on two faces; for reed 1.26 rad, not self-locking, slip near 35 N), and the release check needs that slip load above the 5 N dressing pull and tails of at least 0.02 m + w, after which the wrap carries 5 N; cord-on-bark friction is a new declared value 0.3 for reed on dry branch bark (the low end of dry fiber rope on wood), and bark-on-bark friction is not represented and resists nothing, which understates holding; a trial puts one hand on each piece, a 0.05 m grip with its inner edge 0.01 m beyond the crossing's footprint on that piece, the wrists supplying any couple; force = min(trialForce, 200 N x health/100, the fiber-cord@1 grip rule 10000 N/m x the narrower piece diameter); separate pulls the pieces apart across the crossing, the wrap tension clamping them until the pull reaches twice it and each side of the wrap then carrying half, against closure slip and the cord breaking force divided by 1 + w/(2 x the tightest arc) (the cord-knot@1 curvature rule), so within the 10 N bound it holds with the clamping force just reaching zero; slide draws the bottom piece along the top one and slips when the force reaches 0.3 x the wrap tension x the wrap's contact angle on the top piece (about 4.3 N for 31.6 mm pieces and a 6.1 mm cord), recorded as a one-cord-width displacement at which the hands stop while the binding stays closed; pieces bend as cantilevers from each grip under the branch law strength; cord extension, creep (the fiber-cord@1 creep law at constant volume, rounded to 0.1 mm), strand damage above half a breaking load and piece bending are recorded; creep becomes slack that lowers the wrap tension by the cord stiffness x slack / wrap, and a wrap at zero tension is a loose binding; between rounds a cord too weak for its own wrap tension parts at the side of the top arc into two owned fragments of conserved length and quantity, and a binding carried by its owner hangs the bottom piece (1.1 mass x 9.81) in the wrap, checked against closure slip and breakage and creeping for one round; untying needs condition 0.5 and a 0.02 m pinch on each tail, and a closure that hugs the other end after a load above half its breaking force jams; the tucked and bound states give the cord the role bound (worn 0.0005 per round here, once, since fiber-cord@1 wears only cords and fragments) and reserve all three items for the binding id, so transfers, knots, joins, straight trials and other work are refused; hand-held stages relax on interruption (a routed wrap falls loose and must be redone, a laid crossing carried away must be laid again, an untie with its closure withdrawn falls open); death stops work, leaves the items where the person died and keeps a tucked or bound relation; released undamaged pieces keep no record, so they stay ordinary branch units. For Wren's actual items the first paid round is a measured shortfall: her 8.1 mm, 0.34 m cords against two 31.6 mm units need 0.4332 m at 90 degrees and 0.4136 m at 30 degrees, no hand-twisted cord exceeds 0.34 m and joined cords are refused here, so no single-cord binding of two whole units is reachable now; routing through an existing join and any other rigid material remain development dependencies. Events crossing-binding-started, -stage, -shortfall, -wrap-routed, -closure-tucked, -release-held, -release-loosened, -relaxed, -paused, -resumed, -cancelled, -stopped, -inspected, -trial, -grip-slipped, -crossing-slipped, -closure-slipped, -damaged, -broken, -loosened, -resisted and -untied carry reusable schematic view metadata (component crossing-binding reusing fiber-cord and cord-knot with recorded provenance: binding and work ids, item ids, crossing point, angle and top direction, piece centres, directions, axis heights, lengths, diameters and condition, the cord's wrap, closure, slack, tails, crossings, schematic centreline and fiber-cord view, grip sites, retention state and the last test, with a completed appearance only for a dressed, release-checked binding); visualComponents is empty. Bounded verified findings use the existing personal records keyed by the functional observation (crossing-wrap-fit, crossing-hand-load, crossing-untie) with item, work and measured values; the release-held event carries no qualified flag, so no milestone, pleasure, satisfaction or comfort follows. Reuse: hand-twist-fiber-cord@1 through FIBER_CORD, hand-tie-cord-knot@1 through CORD_KNOT, and hand-join-fiber-cords@1 through a new append-only CORD_BEND export (cord-bend@1 law, join key, friction, dressing pull and retention rule) inserted before the package object of long-fiber-cord-join.ts; all reused abilities, texts and behavior are unchanged. Tests in apps/simulator/test/long-ex16-hand-bind-crossing.test.ts cover scope and dependencies, learning, size and wording, Wren's actual-size cord on real gathered branch units as a paid measured shortfall, pre-cost refusals, the four paid rounds with a fixture cord lengthened in place to 0.60 m with conserved volume (since no hand-twisted cord reaches the needed length), held, sliding, hand-limited, damaging and breaking outcomes, untying and resistance, pause, relaxation, resume, cancel and loose-binding dressing, inspection, wear, carrying, owner-only rules and death; a local check on the paused round-278 checkpoint showed both of Wren's cords giving that paid shortfall after she gathers two units.
